result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens' sync branch returns the raw fetch `Response` object (`return response;`), while in the normal path GoogleCalendarService previously received a gaxios response with a `.data` property. The new code does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data; ... token.access_token`. In sync mode `res` is a `Response`, so `res.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws; the surrounding try/catch (unchanged) swallows it and falls back to the expired-token auth client. Verified from the diff lines in refreshOAuthTokens.ts and CalendarService.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then treats the returned value as an axios-style object: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true. A `Response` has no `.data` field, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime in sync mode. The finding’s core failure mode is directly verifiable from the diff.
